gap: Residents to move per nursing home
affects: medical transport demand from care facilities
detail: CMS 'Average Number of Residents per Day', an average not the census on the day. Daily census (CMS Payroll Based Journal) is not loaded.

gap: Residents needing a stretcher or wheelchair vehicle
affects: vehicle type mix for care-facility evacuation
detail: CMS MDS 3.0 frequency report is state-level only (not loaded): apply as a labelled range per home.

gap: Generator, fuel and evacuation-agreement status of each nursing home
affects: shelter-in-place vs evacuate decision per facility
detail: Not in CMS provider files. Ask the facility or the state survey agency.

gap: Assisted living communities and personal care homes are not in care_facilities
affects: medically dependent population outside nursing homes
detail: assisted_living from GaMap2Care (Georgia DCH), facility fields only. Homes with 6 or fewer beds carry no name or address and sit at their tract centroid. Licensed beds, not residents.

gap: Home health and hospice agencies serving people at home
affects: medically dependent population at home
detail: overture_places (Overture Maps, per-row licence kept): listings only, no caseload or service area. CMS Home Health and Hospice provider files (US Government work) are the next source; not fetched.

gap: NEMT, para-transit and ambulance fleet
affects: transport capacity for medically dependent evacuees
detail: overture_places locates operators, never fleet size or wheelchair vans; NPPES type-2 provider records (US Government work) are another operator list, not fetched. Fleet is a labelled low/base/high input until a county or state inventory is supplied.

gap: Distance from each facility to a usable medical-needs shelter
affects: medical sheltering access per facility
detail: Computed read-only from the raw snapshot shelters (is_medical): pending teammate shelters_clean.

gap: Dialysis centers without coordinates
affects: distance from dialysis patients to an operating center; center flood exposure
detail: Census Geocoder (US Government work), match quality in coordinates_confidence. Unmatched: Maps place_id lookup at runtime.

gap: emPOWER counts 1-10 published as 11
affects: dialysis, oxygen and home-health demand in small counties
detail: Carried as the range 1-11 (<field>_live_low = 1, value = 11, status imputed).

gap: Snapshot dialysis-like column disagrees with the live service
affects: dialysis and power-dependent demand
detail: Live emPOWER is canonical and carried beside the snapshot; the snapshot column is marked suspect.

gap: Power dependence is county-level
affects: where in a county power-dependent residents live
detail: emPOWER ZIP counts exist (extdata/emPOWER/empower_ga_zip.csv), not joined. Never assign to a block.

gap: Storm-surge inundation by category
affects: which facilities and tracts flood in a given storm
detail: NRI coastal flood is an annualised composite, and GEMA evacuation zones (now on hazard_tracts, care_facilities and assisted_living) are planning zones, not inundation. NOAA NHC SLOSH MOM rasters (public domain) are documented in extdata/slosh, not clipped.

gap: Which shelters are open, full or closed now
affects: operational shelter capacity during an event
detail: GEMA WebEOC feed had no rows when fetched; gema_shelter_feed is its facility and status schema, an input for the teammate shelters table. Contact, phone and remarks fields are never read. FEMA OpenShelters total_population is a live query only.

gap: 2020 tracts with no NRI hazard row
affects: nothing while population is 0 (water tracts)
detail: Asserted at build: the build fails if any populated tract lacks a row.

gap: Which shelters actually open in an incident
affects: shelter-opening probability per shelter
detail: FEMA NSS last-activation layer (US Government work), 1:1 on shelter_id. Only the most recent activation per shelter survives, so earlier openings are lost.

gap: Shelter fill and occupancy in past storms
affects: shelter demand against capacity
detail: No shelter-level history. NSS populations are a lower bound (status reported_lower_bound). Anchor a labelled range on Red Cross statewide peaks once their releases are cited; live occupancy only from the GEMA feed during an incident.

gap: Activated shelters with no readiness data
affects: shelter capacity and opening evidence
detail: Real activations: status activated_readiness_unrecorded, kept as opening evidence and never counted as extra seats.

gap: Whether a shelter is rated for hurricane use
affects: which shelters can be used before landfall
detail: No ARC 4496 or FEMA P-361 rating in any source. Fill: NSS hurricane-activation evidence (proven, excluded, unknown) plus Maps verification of the largest unknowns; the shelters table itself is owned by a teammate.

gap: Warning lead time by storm origin
affects: evacuation window per scenario
detail: analysis/flow storm library: first NWS VTEC watch and warning for any Georgia zone to Georgia tropical-storm-wind onset (NHC best track), our calculation.

gap: Evacuation order timing and areas
affects: departure start time per county
detail: OpenFEMA IPAWS holds no Georgia coastal evacuation order before 2022 (none for Matthew, Irma, Michael or Dorian). evac_orders takes Matthew, Irma and Dorian from cited governor releases. Gulf storms (Michael, Helene, Milton, Isaias 2026): no coastal mandatory order found, unverified.

gap: Official clearance times from the Hurricane Evacuation Study
affects: how long the coast needs to clear
detail: Published only in HURREVAC, which is restricted to emergency managers.

gap: Power outage extent and duration per storm
affects: when power-dependent residents become an emergency
detail: County storm outages from EAGLE-I (ORNL, CC BY 4.0) as published by the grid analysis (analysis/grid county_storm_outages), used by the storm library; DOE OE-417 filings in outage_events. The trigger is county outage share, not coastal zone.

gap: Departure-timing curve
affects: congestion and clearance time
detail: Not in hand: a labelled curve from cited departure-timing studies (Matthew).

gap: Florida inflow competing for Georgia capacity
affects: Georgia medical seats, dialysis chairs and I-75/I-16 load in Gulf and NE Florida scenarios
detail: Florida snapshot tables; analysis/flow scenarios (b) and (c).

gap: Dialysis schedule cohort (MWF or TTS)
affects: which patients miss a session for a given landfall day
detail: Not published: half and half, swept 40-60%.

gap: Staff available at dialysis centers, nursing homes and shelters
affects: usable capacity when staff evacuate too
detail: Not published: a labelled range correlated with storm category.

gap: Evacuation mortality risk for nursing-home residents
affects: evacuate or shelter in place per facility
detail: Range from cited post-Rita and Gustav cohort studies.

gap: Shelter failure in the storm (power, roof, cooling, water)
affects: post-impact capacity
detail: Florida after-action documents give failure modes, not rates: a labelled range.

gap: Time to harm: portable oxygen, dialysis interval, shelter stay
affects: time-to-harm per person type
detail: Clinical norms, cited.

gap: Official evacuation route geometry
affects: which roads evacuees use
detail: GDOT hurricane evacuation routes and contraflow route are the corridor layer in analysis/flow (cleared with attribution); TIGER/Line covers I-75 north of Macon and I-20, which GDOT's layer omits. GEMA I-16 contraflow intersections are in contraflow_intersections.
